title: Closing the gap in men’s health: Hims launches testosterone care in the UK
summary: At-home blood collection and personalised treatment options give eligible men across the UK a simpler path to testosterone care
body_markdown:
Low testosterone is more common among men in the UK than most may realise. In a major study led by researchers at the University of Manchester, around 1 in 7 men aged 40 to 79 in the UK and across Europe were found to have low testosterone levels.¹ For many men, symptoms are easy to dismiss. A fading sex drive, constant tiredness, low mood or a thickening waistline tend to get blamed on stress, work or simply getting older, and many men push through for years without finding out what’s behind them.


In a new survey of UK men commissioned by Hims, 68% of respondents said taboos about testosterone use are “strong” or “very strong.”² Even when men decide to get checked, getting care can be harder than it should be. For some, the nearest appointment is far from home or hard to fit around work. In the same survey, 78% of men said they are curious to know what their testosterone levels are, but only 21% have had a blood test to check them.³ Over my career, I’ve seen how these barriers lead men to wait until small concerns become bigger ones.


Today, that changes. Hims is launching testosterone care in the UK for clinically eligible men.


Every man starts with a clinical assessment and a blood test, and if treatment is appropriate, a UK-registered GP will recommend a personalised plan that may include oral or topical options tailored to his health and care needs. These new treatment plans from Hims are designed to help support a man’s natural testosterone production, rather than replace it. For men who also experience sexual symptoms, a combination treatment is available.


Hims is making it easier for men to navigate and take charge of their health proactively, removing the everyday friction and barriers they’ve faced for years. Men experiencing symptoms can check their testosterone with a single blood sample, collected at home using the[Tasso® device](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cmaDHPOCu6k) , a push-button collector worn on the upper arm. Hims is the first platform in the UK to offer Testosterone treatments that can start from a single at-home blood sample, with no finger-pricking and no follow-up clinic visit.


Here’s what the process looks like for customers:


- **One sample, a fuller picture of health.** Men collect one small sample at home and send it to our partner lab. From that sample, the lab tests a broad panel of biomarkers, so a GP can look at testosterone in the context of a man’s wider health, not just a single number.
- **Reviewed by a UK-registered GP.** Every customer completes a detailed medical questionnaire, and a GP reviews his symptoms, history and test results.
- **Personalised treatment, when it’s needed.** If treatment is clinically appropriate, a GP will put together a personalised plan that may include oral or topical treatment options tailored to the individual. Treatment is only prescribed after a clinical assessment and blood results, and only when a GP judges it appropriate.
- **Care that continues.** Men on a treatment plan get follow-up testing, regular check-ins, and access to our clinical team, so their plan can be adjusted as results and symptoms change.
- **Keeping his own GP in the loop.** With a customer’s consent, results and treatment plans can be shared with his GP, so his health record stays complete.


Despite common stereotypes, for a majority of men, this isn’t about bulking up. In our survey, 80% of UK respondents said they prioritize more energy over more muscle.⁴ They want to get through the workday, keep up with their kids and feel like themselves. Checking testosterone is often one of the first steps toward that, and understanding what’s behind how they’ve been feeling opens the door to acting on it, whether that means treatment, changes to sleep, diet or exercise, or simply peace of mind. Because low testosterone is linked to other critical conditions, including type 2 diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular disease,⁵ ⁶ a single blood test can also be a useful first step in looking at a man’s wider health, not just his hormones.


With testosterone care now available in the UK, Hims is offering men access to simple, clinically guided care that helps them take a more proactive approach to their health.
